A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRiSM benchmark. The complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original phone-recognition and downstream evaluation results in Tables 3–4, plus masking, inventory-induction, geolocation, and thinking-mode analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds layer-selection, few-shot prompting, score-weighting, and error-distribution analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix F adds a representation-probe variant using a learnable weighted sum across all model layers, whereas v1 evaluates only last-layer representations. This changes one probe component; the default PRiSM framework, transcript probe, and recognition models remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Tables 1 and 5 retain the same intrinsic and downstream datasets, tasks, languages, and populations. The added experiments vary probing and prompting procedures within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator roster is unchanged, including the specialized PR models, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Qwen3-Omni-Instruct, WavLM, Whisper, and naive baseline. The new analyses evaluate existing models under additional settings.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with all-layer RP experiments, Qwen 1-shot/5-shot/N-shot and Gemini N-shot evaluations, and four alternative score-weighting schemes assessed through ranking agreement. These are additional protocols in Appendices B.2, F, and G; the original benchmark splits, metrics, and default probe settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial sensitivity analyses for representation-layer selection, few-shot prompting, and aggregate-score weighting. Section 5.1 also adds a DoReCo error-outlier breakdown. The original masking, inventory-induction, geolocation, and thinking-mode analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 4 retains mean ± standard deviation across five random seeds where applicable. The additions provide means, point results, and descriptive ranking correlations, without adding or revising repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The original Tables 3–4 and Figures 2–5 are unchanged, but Tables 7–8 add substantial results under new conditions. For example, W2V2P-LV60 scores 34.9 on GEO-v with weighted-layer RP versus 24.6 with last-layer RP; Qwen's LID-fl score is 59.1 zero-shot versus 14.4–14.6 few-shot. New weighting-stability and PFER-tail findings further expand the reported evidence.

T1.justification: The PFER equation, phone-inventory metric definition, and logarithmically weighted aggregate-score equation are unchanged. The added empirical sensitivity checks introduce no new theoretical assumptions, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and principal claims about language exposure, encoder-CTC stability, and LALMs trailing specialized PR models. New experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 materially revises several explanations: Section 5.1 attributes extreme LALM averages to unstable outliers and expands the existing unseen-language caveat; Section 6.1 emphasizes output dependencies and CR-CTC noise consistency, removing the Zipformer bottleneck hypothesis. Section 3.2 qualifies TP/RP comparisons, and the new appendices interpret layer and prompting sensitivity.

D1.justification: Appendix G defines N-shot as one example per class and documents Gemini's resource constraint. Table 5 changes EdAcc's stated license from CC BY 4.0 to CC BY-SA 4.0. Existing probe hyperparameters, hardware and compute descriptions, preprocessing instructions, and access links are retained.

R1.justification: The substantive cited-work coverage and research positioning are unchanged. Bibliographic revisions update publication metadata and consolidate duplicate references to Speechocean762 and L2-ARCTIC; these do not introduce or remove distinct research works.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites in Sections 3.2, 5.1, and 6.1, added appendix explanations, and reordered appendices, including moving prompts from Appendix D to I. Affiliation, acknowledgment, terminology, and bibliography edits accompany these changes, while most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7–8 for layer-fusion and few-shot results, including mean/change and shot-count displays. Existing figures and Tables 1–6 are retained; Table 6, Figure 5, and prompt boxes move within the reordered appendices. The overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: The added layer, prompting, and weighting checks strengthen the benchmark's evidential support, while revised explanations better qualify LALM failures and architectural effects. These gains are tempered by a new inconsistency: Appendix F says no model improves across every task, although Table 7 shows positive changes throughout for W2V2P-LV60 and POWSM-CTC. Overall, the revision provides a limited net improvement in robustness and interpretability.
